question: What is the main goal of a nursing interview with a patient?

options.B: To provide psychotherapy for mental illness
options.C: To gather health data and assess needs

explanation: You've got this! Think of a nursing interview as a friendly chat to collect information about the patient's health status and personal history so you can care for them properly. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: How does nursing counselling differ from a regular patient interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on empowering patients to cope with health challenges
options.B: Counselling only occurs during the admission phase of care
options.C: Interviewing requires psychological training whereas counselling does not
options.D: Interviewing is strictly for doctors while counselling is for nurses

explanation: While interviews gather facts, counselling goes a step further. It helps patients emotionally adjust and find the strength to cope with their health situations. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: What does active listening truly mean when talking to a patient?

options.A: Maintaining silence until the patient finishes speaking entirely
options.B: Writing down every word the patient speaks verbatim
options.C: Interrupting frequently to ask clarifying medical questions
options.D: Paying attention to both verbal messages and body language

explanation: Active listening is more than just hearing words. It means tuning in fully to what they say *and* what their body language is telling you. Great nursing is all about these details! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a good example of an open-ended question?

options.A: Did you take your prescribed blood pressure medication today?
options.B: Is your surgical wound draining any yellow fluid?
options.C: Are you experiencing any sharp chest pain right now?
options.D: How have you been feeling since your last clinic visit?

explanation: Open-ended questions invite the patient to share their story rather than just giving a quick 'yes' or 'no'. It helps you build a much better picture of their health! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: During which phase of an interview does a nurse build initial rapport and explain why they are there?
explanation: Think of the orientation phase as your warm introduction. It sets a comfortable tone, introduces who you are, and explains the purpose of the chat. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the working phase during a patient interview?

options.A: To schedule future clinic appointments for medication refills
options.B: To summarize the entire conversation and say goodbye
options.C: To actively gather health data using targeted questions
options.D: To introduce the healthcare team to the patient's family

explanation: The working phase is the heart of the assessment, where you actively dive in and gather all the necessary health information. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is a key feature of a professional, therapeutic nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It is centered entirely on the patient's health needs
options.B: It focuses equally on the personal problems of both individuals
options.C: It is designed to last indefinitely as a social friendship
options.D: It allows the nurse to make personal demands on the patient

explanation: Unlike normal friendships, therapeutic relationships are strictly professional and focus solely on promoting the patient's healing and well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to maintain professional boundaries during counselling?

options.A: To avoid having to listen to personal stories from patients
options.B: To ensure the patient pays for nursing services promptly
options.C: To protect the objectivity of care and prevent emotional burnout
options.D: To keep the doctor from interfering with the patient's care plan

explanation: Boundaries keep you safe from emotional exhaustion and help you stay clear-headed and professional so you can give the best care possible. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT an environmental barrier to good communication?

options.A: Lack of privacy in a crowded room

explanation: Anxiety comes from within the patient, making it a psychological barrier. Noise, lack of privacy, and staff interruptions are all things in the physical environment around them. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h5)

question: How should you handle a language barrier when counselling a patient?

options.A: Ask a passing visitor to translate the entire medical history
options.B: Speak much louder in English so the patient eventually catches on
options.C: Skip the health history and rely only on laboratory test results
options.D: Use a qualified medical interpreter to ensure accurate exchange

explanation: Always go for a trained medical interpreter! It keeps clinical details accurate and protects the patient's right to privacy, unlike random bystanders. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h5)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the patient's condition is interesting to other nurses
options.B: When there is a legal duty to report suspected child abuse
options.C: When the nurse wants to discuss a case with a close friend
options.D: When a family member demands to know the diagnosis

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred, but the law requires us to break it when vulnerable lives are at risk—such as reporting suspected abuse or severe public harm. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h6)

question: What does obtaining 'informed consent' actually mean during patient care?

options.A: Convincing the patient to accept the doctor's orders without question
options.B: Having the patient sign a form without reading it during admission
options.C: Obtaining permission from the head of the hospital for treatment
options.D: Ensuring the patient understands the risks and benefits before agreeing

explanation: Informed consent means the patient truly understands what they are walking into—including pros and cons—and freely agrees to the care plan. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h6)
